sources.title: Find an energy certificate
sources.verified_claim: The official service can locate existing EPC, DEC and air-conditioning certificates by postcode, street/town or certificate number. Certificate availability or rating is not inferred for a sample parcel without an exact property match.

sources.title: Get energy performance of buildings data
sources.verified_claim: The current government bulk-data service provides domestic and non-domestic EPC and DEC data by CSV and API, including certificates that may have expired or been replaced. Bulk availability is not exact candidate evidence without address/title matching.

sources.title: Energy Performance of Buildings Certificates
sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.verified_claim: The official collection is the publication route for EPC/DEC statistics, live tables, technical notes and change notes. Aggregate publications do not establish a candidate property's current EPC.

sources.title: Energy Performance of Building Certificates in England and Wales: January to March 2026
sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.verified_claim: Q1 2026 EPC statistics were revised after a local-authority allocation processing error. The revision caveat is retained and aggregate statistics are not converted into parcel ratings.

sources.title: Domestic private rented property: minimum energy efficiency standard - landlord guidance
sources.publisher: Department for Energy Security and Net Zero
sources.verified_claim: Current domestic MEES guidance requires covered privately rented homes to meet at least EPC E unless a valid exemption applies; the page also notes future policy work. Coverage depends on tenancy and EPC facts that are not yet bound to a sample parcel.

sources.title: Non-domestic private rented property: minimum energy efficiency standard - landlord guidance
sources.publisher: Department for Energy Security and Net Zero
sources.verified_claim: Covered non-domestic rented property must generally meet EPC E unless exempt. Applicability depends on the actual premises and tenancy; no candidate use or EPC is invented.

sources.title: View private rented sector energy standards exemptions
sources.publisher: Department for Energy Security and Net Zero
sources.verified_claim: The official register can be searched for MEES exemptions and penalties by property or landlord details. No exemption is assumed for a sample parcel without an exact search.

sources.title: Improving the energy performance of privately rented homes: 2025 update
sources.publisher: Department for Energy Security and Net Zero
sources.verified_claim: Government's response sets a single 1 October 2030 compliance date for the future domestic PRS standard and a new metric framework. Future requirements are not treated as current EPC compliance for the sample parcels.
